source_described_scope_or_purpose.content: Benchmark proposal shifts evaluation from optimization within a fixed representation to evolution of the representation itself.
The document introduces candidate metrics as operational tools for studying representation lifecycles, not final universal equations.
Framework studies intelligence as temporary expansion followed by compression into simpler representations preserving important structure.
Explicit source boundaries: no consciousness theory, no specific AI architecture, no replacement of information theory/Bayesian inference/MDL, and no claim that every adaptive system is intelligent.

source_role_branches.source_variant_payload: Framework does not propose a specific AI architecture.
Framework does not claim every adaptive system is intelligent.
Framework does not claim to explain consciousness.
Framework does not replace information theory, Bayesian inference, or MDL.
Architect Intelligence is not proposed as a new AI architecture.

definitions_and_formal_structures.content: An invariant is a relationship stable despite changes in observation, representation, or conditions.
Predictive sufficiency is approximated by P(Y|X)≈P(Y|phi(X)); representation removes irrelevant information while retaining predictive ability.
Productive complexity is temporary exploration through new measurements, representations, experiments and scaffolding.
Representation phi:X→Z maps observations to internal structure, with L(phi) denoting representation construction/maintenance complexity.

source_role_branches.source_variant_payload: Representation mapping phi:X→Z transforms observed world X into internal representation Z.
phi:X→Z compresses observations into usable structure and L(phi) measures construction/maintenance complexity.
L(phi) is the description/operation complexity cost of representation phi:X→Z.

definitions_and_formal_structures.content: Representation Elasticity denotes temporary complexity expansion followed by much smaller permanent retained complexity after compression.

source_role_branches.source_variant_payload: Representation Elasticity is the ability to temporarily increase complexity and later compress it into permanent simplification.
E = ΔC_expanded/ΔC_permanent, with high elasticity meaning temporary expansion greatly exceeds permanent retained complexity.

definitions_and_formal_structures.content: Δ_U = [L(T_A)+L(T_B)]-[L(T*)+L(phi_A)+L(phi_B)] includes mapping costs when judging unification.
Compression gain Δ_C = L(T_raw)-L(T*) measures reduction after discovering an invariant.
Repeated elasticity ratio comparing temporary expansion cost with permanent retained complexity; source occurrences differ in role and candidate standing.

source_role_branches.source_variant_payload: Elasticity E = ΔC_expanded / ΔC_permanent.
E = ΔC_expanded/ΔC_permanent measures temporary complexity relative to permanent retained complexity.
Representation elasticity intuition E = temporary complexity absorbed / permanent complexity added.

Search for a new representation whose explanatory-efficiency score exceeds the current representation.

Minimize L(phi) subject to P(Y|phi(X))≥P_target.

assertions_or_hypotheses_and_interpretat.content: Benchmarking intelligence should measure representation evolution because scientific progress can come from finding simpler representations.
The Elastic Mind uses complexity temporarily and reaches generalization through expansion, understanding and compression.
The source orders abstraction from observation to pattern to invariant to generative model.
The source repeatedly describes an elastic lifecycle of expansion under anomaly, invariant/structure discovery, compression, prediction, failure, and representation update.

source_role_branches.source_variant_payload: Flexible intelligence uses expansion for observation/tools, discovery for invariants/causal structure, and compression to remove unnecessary complexity.
Intelligence is managing creation, refinement and replacement of models across reality→observation→representation→prediction→failure→update.
Intelligence is primarily the ability to manage the lifecycle of representations: expand, extract invariants, compress, and replace inefficient representations.
The elastic cycle is unknown structure→expansion→invariant discovery→compression→minimal model→new unknown structure.
Elastic intelligence expands when reality becomes more complex, compresses after structure discovery, and restructures inefficient representations.
Framework lifecycle is Reality→Observation→Expansion→Invariant Discovery→Compression→Prediction→Failure→Representation Update.
Elastic systems expand representation under unknown structure, extract invariants, compress scaffolding, and repeat after new anomalies.
Representation Elasticity frames intelligence as management of model lifecycles through observation, prediction, failure and representation update.

assertions_or_hypotheses_and_interpretat.content: The preferred representation is not merely smallest; it minimizes complexity while preserving sufficient predictive performance.

source_role_branches.source_variant_payload: The target is maximum predictive power per unit of representation complexity, not maximum retained information.
The target is the simplest representation that preserves prediction, not the smallest possible representation.

assertions_or_hypotheses_and_interpretat.content: Representation change is proposed when exceptions/patch cost and reduced explanatory efficiency indicate the current coordinate system has become the bottleneck.

source_role_branches.source_variant_payload: Scientific revolutions may occur when the framework itself, rather than search within it, is the bottleneck.
Every representation has a domain of validity and begins to fail when maintaining it requires increasing correction.
Highest elasticity includes replacing the coordinate system when anomalies and patch cost make the current representation inefficient.
A mature system should detect when representation itself becomes the bottleneck and may replace the descriptive coordinate system rather than add complexity.

assertions_or_hypotheses_and_interpretat.content: Source-described failure modes include premature compression, permanent expansion, uncontrolled complexity, hoarding, ignoring complexity, and permanent patch accumulation.

source_role_branches.source_variant_payload: Unhealthy learning is proposed as anomaly→permanent patches→more exceptions→model collapse.
Permanent expansion accumulates parameters, exceptions, rules and specialized mechanisms, reducing generalization and increasing scaffolding dependence.
Premature compression ignores important variables, misses anomalies and prevents adaptation.
The Hoarder keeps observations/tools and becomes a database of experiences rather than a model.
The Ignorer deletes complexity before understanding it and produces an incorrect oversimplified model.
Uncontrolled complexity is characterized by patches, parameters, special cases and fragility.

assertions_or_hypotheses_and_interpretat.content: Tools are treated as temporary scaffolding whose value lies in producing observations that can be internalized so dependency can later be removed.

source_role_branches.source_variant_payload: Tool value depends on whether observations produced by the tool become an internal predictive model rather than a permanent external dependency.
Optimal scaffolding is temporary dependence followed by independence after structure discovery.
A tool is successful when it changes what the system can understand; tool dependence should eventually become optional after internalization.
Tool metabolism distinguishes Tool→Decision→Action dependence from Tool→Observation→Internal Model→Prediction internalization.

assertions_or_hypotheses_and_interpretat.content: Core source hypothesis: intelligence consists in repeatedly finding lower-complexity representations that preserve or improve predictive/generative power.

source_role_branches.source_variant_payload: Higher intelligence is characterized by repeatedly discovering simpler, more powerful representations, so benchmarks should reward improvement of internal languages.
Intelligence is the ability to discover representations where less information is sufficient.
A truly intelligent system discovers representations requiring the least information while preserving predictive power.
Intelligence temporarily absorbs complexity, extracts invariant structure, and returns with a simpler model of reality.
Best intelligence is the smallest representation that preserves structure required to generate future predictions.
Highest intelligence repeatedly transforms complexity into simpler, more powerful representations.
Intelligence is the ability to discover representations where less information is sufficient, rather than the ability to store more information.

assertions_or_hypotheses_and_interpretat.content: Framework proposes a unifying hypothesis about adaptive epistemic dynamics.
Large positive Δ_C is presented as successful theoretical compression.
Failure after scaffolding removal indicates interface dependence; survival indicates underlying structure learned; creating better scaffolding under change indicates learning-to-learn.
High elasticity converts substantial exploratory complexity into small permanent cost; low elasticity leaves much of the added complexity in place.

source_role_branches.source_variant_payload: High elasticity converts large exploration cost into small permanent increase; low elasticity retains the complexity.
E≫1 indicates high elasticity; E≈1 indicates exploration without effective metabolization.
High elasticity combines large exploratory expansion with small final representation cost and improved prediction; low elasticity leaves permanent accumulated complexity.

assertions_or_hypotheses_and_interpretat.content: Failure is information about limits of the current representation, not merely an error.
Forgetting-test outcomes are interpreted as dependence under collapse, structural capture under stability, and successful noise removal under improvement.

source_role_branches.source_variant_payload: Performance collapse indicates dependence on removed information.
Improved performance is interpreted as removed information being primarily noise and the representation identifying minimal sufficient information.
Stable performance is interpreted as capture of underlying structure.

assertions_or_hypotheses_and_interpretat.content: High fertility means a small theory generates many novel consequences.
A strong scientific representation should compress domains, generate predictions, survive transformations and require minimal complexity.
Strong learners expand, discover and contract efficiently; weak learners expand indefinitely.
Tool-metabolism index interpretations distinguish dependence (near 0), retained performance after removal (near 1), and possible improvement after removal (>1).

source_role_branches.source_variant_payload: M≈0 denotes dependence on the tool.
M>1 is interpreted as improvement after removing distracting unnecessary tooling.
M≈1 denotes retained performance after tool removal.

methodology_or_test_protocol.content: A true abstraction is proposed to satisfy Δ_U>0, so unification must be cheaper after mapping costs.
Proposed benchmark dimensions evaluate compression, invariance, generalization, and the ability to revise or replace the representation itself.

source_role_branches.source_variant_payload: Reward reduction in description length rather than memorization.
Use zero-shot, counterfactual, out-of-distribution and novel-combination tasks to assess representation fertility.
Test whether learned structure survives superficial transformations such as notation, coordinates, order, language or interface.
Test whether the model detects representation failure and replaces an inefficient coordinate system rather than endlessly patching it.

methodology_or_test_protocol.content: After domain structure is discovered, remove unnecessary information and test whether performance is maintained or improved.
Learn from full observations, remove 90–99% of observations, then retest.
A robust abstraction should approximately satisfy T(X)≈T(h(X)) under input transformations.
Proposed paradigm-shift diagnostics compare patch/adaptation growth against a threshold and require a better-scoring alternative representation.

source_role_branches.source_variant_payload: Paradigm shift trigger is proposed when adaptation-cost growth dA_n/dn>δ and a new representation phi_2 exists with Ω(phi_2)>Ω(phi_1).
Replacement is proposed when patch cost exceeds rebuild cost and adaptation-cost growth dA_n/dn exceeds δ.

methodology_or_test_protocol.content: Proposed diagnostics use growing exceptions/patches, declining explanatory power, maintenance burden, and anomaly-driven complexity trajectories to identify representation failure.

source_role_branches.source_variant_payload: Healthy learning is proposed as anomaly→temporary complexity→invariant discovery→simpler permanent model.
Growing exceptions, special cases, external support and reduced generalization are proposed symptoms of representation failure.
More patches plus less explanatory power plus increasing maintenance cost is proposed as a representation-failure warning signal.

methodology_or_test_protocol.content: Introduce situations where current models become inefficient and test whether the system voluntarily replaces its representation.
Use environments with hidden variables, latent symmetries, causal mechanisms and compact explanations, rewarding discovery rather than known-answer reproduction.
Successful agents should show increasing compression, stable invariance, growing generative ability, decreasing tool dependence and periodic representation replacement.
Measure performance after tool removal to distinguish internalized understanding from external dependency.

applications_or_examples.content: Possible domains include synthetic physics, cellular automata, unknown programming languages, procedural games, symbolic systems, mathematics and simulated ecosystems.
Examples include coordinate-independent physics, notation-independent identities and presentation-independent causal mechanisms.
Examples include conservation laws, notation-independent mathematics, shared biological mechanisms and cross-environment strategies.
Potential applications include AI agents, scientific discovery, theorem discovery, representation learning, cognitive modeling and adaptive planning.

open_questions.content: Open research questions concern novel predictions, autonomous representation replacement, separation from intervention evolution, external constraints, objective evolution, evolutionary analogues, compatibility with existing theories, and distinguishing benchmarks.

source_role_branches.source_variant_payload: Can representation evolution be formally separated from intervention evolution?
Is an external constraint system the true compass of intelligence?
Can objectives themselves evolve without collapsing into arbitrary self-reference?
Does evolution instantiate the same algorithm?
Can this framework reproduce existing results in active learning, MDL, Bayesian model selection, and scientific discovery?
What experimental benchmark would distinguish Architect Intelligence from current foundation models?
Can artificial systems autonomously discover, compress and replace their own representations when inadequate?
